I've tried to think of ways to remedy this with homebrew. To remain constant with 5e's overarching goal of streamlining, at the moment I believe the best way to achieve this is to attach properties to each damage type. Piercing weapons roll an extra damage die even resolving critical damage. Slashing weapons do an extra 2 damage against unarmored or lightly armored targets. When using bludgeoning weapons (not fists), opponents in heavy armor have their AC reduced by one for the purposes of resolving the hit.

Really solid ideas.

I think a better way of doing it would be:

Slashing: Bonus damage die equal to the excess in the hit, rounded down with a minimum of 1 damage. If you were in excess of 1-3, add one damage. 4-5, add a 1d4. 6-7, add a 1d6. 8-9 is a 1d8, and 10+ adds a 1d10.
For example, you rolled 20 against 15 AC. You rolled 5 in excess, so add the highest damage die that's equal or lower the excess, which is a 1d4. Best on unarmored enemies.

Pierce: Take the lowest number you can crit on and subtract it by 1. Makes impossible-to-hit enemies easier to hit, and sometimes gives you a lucky break when you need it.

Bludgeoning: Add half of your proficiency (rounded down) to your to-hit. Helps deal with all units, but armored ones especially.

I feel like this can scale a bit better than some of yours, especially considering there may be difficulty classing the armor type of a bear or dragon. But I definitely used yours as inspiration. Mine definitely has more power creep than yours, so yours would definitely be better for a more 'subtle' solution that doesn't risk breaking the game.

The extra damage on crit would be rare, and only really be used by Champions (and it would be weird for all Champions to want to use spears, with no lore to back it up). 2 flat damage for the entire duration of the game won't be balanced well at different points. The bludgeoning one isn't bad, except for the armor classing bit.

From playing games with weapon types, it seems to boil down to these three things:

Pierce is good for killing anything, soft or hard.

Slash is great for killing things that don't have armor, and is useless for things that do.

Bludgeoning is good for things that have armor, but aren't always as big of a threat.

And for that, we both seem to agree. I'm worried stuff like this might overcomplicate the flow of combat. But I guess it's better than just having everything be the same or RPing every little hit people do.

I like your ideas on slashing and piercing. I'm wary of increasing the to-hit bonus from bludgeoning by more than one, however, as bounded accuracy makes even that +1 difference non-trivial, however. Adding two or more has the potential to really mess with balance.

You're right. I just don't know how to deal with it without making it useless. Maybe subtract 10% of the target's AC, rounded down? There aren't too many enemies with 20 AC to get the -2 effectiveness.

Alternatively, bludgeoning weapons get advantage on the "Shove" action.
